# CodeAtlas Individual Contributor License Agreement

**Version 1.0 — 2026-10-03**

Thank you for contributing to CodeAtlas. This agreement clarifies the
intellectual property license granted with contributions from any person or
entity. It protects you as much as it protects the project: it puts in writing
what you have agreed to, so that nobody can later claim you agreed to something
else.

You keep the copyright to your contribution. This is a licence, **not an
assignment**. You can continue to use your own work however you like, including
in other projects under other licences.

This document is adapted from the Apache Software Foundation Individual
Contributor License Agreement v2.0, which is the common form for this purpose.

## Definitions

**"You"** means the individual who submits a Contribution, or the legal entity
authorising it. For a legal entity, "You" includes entities that control, are
controlled by, or are under common control with that entity.

**"Project Owner"** means Vamsi Krishna Kanneganti (GitHub: `vamsikk7`), the copyright holder of CodeAtlas.

**"Contribution"** means any original work of authorship — including
modifications and additions to existing work — that You intentionally submit to
the Project Owner for inclusion in CodeAtlas. "Submit" means any form of
communication sent to the Project Owner or its repositories, including pull
requests, patches, issues containing code, and electronic mail, but excluding
anything you clearly mark in writing as "Not a Contribution".

## 2. Patent licence

You grant the Project Owner, and to recipients of software distributed by the

If any entity institutes patent litigation alleging that Your Contribution, or

## 3. Relicensing — please read this section

You grant the Project Owner the right to license Your Contribution under terms
of the Project Owner's choosing, **including proprietary or commercial terms**,
in addition to the Apache License 2.0.

This is the clause that makes [COMMERCIAL.md](../COMMERCIAL.md) meaningful, and
it is the one most worth understanding before you sign.

What it means in practice: a feature you contribute may later appear in a
commercially licensed CodeAtlas product, and you would not receive payment or a
separate say in that.

What it does not mean: it does not remove your contribution from the open
source project. Code released under Apache-2.0 stays available under
Apache-2.0, permanently, for you and for everyone else. Relicensing adds a
licence; it cannot take the open one away.

If this clause is unacceptable to you, that is a reasonable position and you
should not sign. Please still open issues and participate — a CLA is required
only for code contributions.

## 4. Your representations

You represent that:

1. You are legally entitled to grant the above licences.
2. Each Contribution is Your original creation, or You have the necessary
   rights to submit it.
3. **If your employer has rights to intellectual property you create**, you
   have either received permission to make the Contribution on their behalf,
   your employer has waived those rights, or your employer has executed the
   [Corporate CLA](CLA-CORPORATE.md). This matters more than people expect —
   many employment contracts claim ownership of code written by employees, even
   outside work hours.
4. Any third-party material included in a Contribution is identified as such,
   complete with its source and licence.

## 5. No warranty and no obligation

You provide Your Contributions on an "AS IS" basis, without warranties or
conditions of any kind, express or implied — except for the representations in
section 4, which you do make knowingly.

The Project Owner is under no obligation to accept, merge, or keep any
Contribution.

## 6. Notification

You agree to notify the Project Owner if you become aware of any fact or
circumstance that would make any of these representations inaccurate.

## How to sign

Open a pull request. The CLA Assistant bot will comment with a link, and
signing takes one click. Your signature is recorded against your GitHub
account and covers all your future contributions — you sign once, not per pull
request.
